# references.md backfill — per-batch agent instructions

Repo: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering (run commands from there).
Skill spec: .claude/skills/papers/SKILL.md (read Steps 2–4 once).

Context: an earlier /papers run marked these papers `integrated` and cited them in notes, but
hit a usage limit before writing their references.md rows. Your batch file lists each paper:
key, arxiv, title, home, pdf (repo-relative), cited_in (notes that cite it; may be another home),
venue, review_status (null = you decide: arXiv-only → preprint).

**Do NOT edit any repo file.** Write a single JSON file of proposals to the output path given
to you. The coordinator applies everything (rows, note fixes, frontmatter sources).

For EACH paper:
1. `grep -n '<arxiv-id>'` each cited_in note; read the citing passage with enough surrounding
   context (and the heading it sits under).
2. Extract the PDF text with
   `uv run -q --with pypdf python -c "import sys,pypdf; r=pypdf.PdfReader(sys.argv[1]); print(len(r.pages),'pages'); print('\n'.join(p.extract_text() for p in r.pages[:int(sys.argv[2])]))" <pdf> 8`
   (more pages, or grep the full text, when the number you need is deeper in). Confirm every
   number, model size, benchmark, and setup the note attributes to the paper, and the
   attribution itself (authors, year, venue, what the paper actually introduced/claimed).
3. If the note is wrong or overstated (wrong number, wrong setup, wrong year/venue,
   attributes an idea the paper doesn't contain), propose a correction as an exact
   old→new string replacement. `old` must be copied verbatim from the file and unique in
   it; keep the note's voice; minimal change. Add a number+setup only if the passage states
   a finding with no number and the fix is one short clause — don't rewrite passages.
   Also propose fixing the citation's venue if it's given wrongly (preprint → "preprint" or date only).
4. Write the references.md row (one sentence finding WITH its number and the setup it holds
   under; add what it doesn't show if short). Exact shapes below.
5. If cited_in is EMPTY: read the paper in full (all pages incl. limitations), decide
   extends / sharpens / skip per the skill, trace origin via
   `sqlite3 scripts/papers/citations.db "SELECT d.title,d.year,d.venue,d.in_repo FROM cites c JOIN work s ON s.id=c.src JOIN work d ON d.id=c.dst WHERE s.arxiv='<id>' AND c.intents LIKE '%methodology%'"`,
   pick the best note+section in the home (read the note in full), and propose the insertion
   as an old→new edit (old = an existing verbatim anchor sentence/paragraph, new = it plus your
   1–3 sentence addition, inline cite style
   `[arXiv:ID](https://arxiv.org/abs/ID) (Author et al., Venue YYYY | YYYY-MM, preprint)`, finding in **bold**).
   If it doesn't hold up, verdict "skip" with a reason.

## Row shapes

### llm-fundamentals home (generative-ai/01-llm-fundamentals/references.md), 5 columns:
`| | Author et al., *Short Title* (Venue YYYY): finding with number and setup | [ID](https://arxiv.org/abs/ID) | ✓ [file.pdf](sources/file.pdf) | [01](notes/01-how-llms-work.md#anchor) |`
- Preprint: `(YYYY ⚑)` instead of `(Venue YYYY)`. A parenthetical alias is fine: `*Adafactor: …* (ICML 2018)`.
- Maps-to links are relative to generative-ai/01-llm-fundamentals/. Other homes, e.g.
  `[mm 06](../../ai-engineering/08-multimodal-engineering/notes/06-generating-images-and-video.md#video)`,
  `[prompt 10](../../ai-engineering/01-prompt-engineering/notes/10-adversarial-prompting.md#anchor)`,
  `[RL 02](../05-RL/notes/02-rlhf-pipeline.md#anchor)`, `[ds 16](../../data-science/notes/16-makemore.md#anchor)`,
  `[eval 04](../../ai-engineering/06-eval/notes/04-graders.md#anchor)`. Link every cited_in note; separate with `, `.
- Anchor = GitHub slug of the heading the citation sits under (lowercase, drop punctuation except `-` and `_`, spaces → `-`; e.g. "The transformer block and the GPT stack" → `the-transformer-block-and-the-gpt-stack`; "Reading a model's size" → `reading-a-models-size`). Copy the heading text into `heading` too so the coordinator can verify.

### 02-style homes (prompt, loop, context), 4 columns:
`| Author et al., [*Title*](https://arxiv.org/abs/ID) (Venue YYYY) | finding with number and setup, one or two sentences | [ID](sources/file.pdf) | [08](notes/08-x.md#anchor) |`
- Preprint: `(Mon YYYY ⚑)`. Links relative to the home folder; other-home links like `[loop 08](../04-loop-engineering/notes/08-self-improving-loops.md#anchor)`, `[eval 03](../06-eval/notes/03-eval-datasets.md#anchor)`.
- Prefix `★ ` to the paper cell only if it changes a claim (contradicts / strong extends).

## Output JSON (a list, one object per paper)
```
{"key": "...", "verdict": "verified|sharpens|corrected|extends|skip",
 "row": "<full markdown row>", "date": "YYYY-MM (arXiv v1)",
 "headings": [{"file": "...", "heading": "..."}],
 "edits": [{"file": "repo-relative path", "old": "...", "new": "...", "why": "what was wrong, per the PDF (page/table)"}],
 "doubts": "anything uncertain, or empty"}
```
verdict: "verified" = note correct as is; "corrected" = you proposed a correction to a wrong claim;
"sharpens"/"extends"/"skip" for empty-cited_in papers. Validate the JSON with
`python3 -c "import json;json.load(open('<out>'))"` before finishing. Reply with a 3-line summary only.
